I am 70 years old and have farmed these fields in Quzhou for 50 years. My father taught me, and I have seen good years and bad. At my age, with just my wife and me in the household, I do not chase new fads or take risks. I stick to the wheat-maize rotation that has always fed us, using my well when the rains fail. I know my 24 mu well — the soil is good alluvial loam, but it needs water at the right time. For winter wheat, I will plant an improved variety in early October after running the rotary tiller through the maize stubble. I put down compound fertilizer as a basal dose and topdress with urea at green-up; too much nitrogen is a waste of money and makes the stalks weak. I irrigate three times: the overwintering water, once at jointing, and once at heading — that is enough if you time it properly. I spray herbicide once and one more spray for insects or mildew if I see it coming. I expect about 750 kg per mu of wheat if the spring is kind.

After cutting wheat in early June, there is no time to lose before the summer rains come. I plant hybrid maize the same day or the next using no-tillage — the less turning of soil in the summer heat, the better. I apply one dose of compound fertilizer at planting and irrigate twice: once when the seedlings are establishing if it is dry, and once at the big trumpet or filling stage when the ears need it most. Two sprays total: herbicide and one for corn borer. I have learned that hybrid seed pays for itself, so I buy good seed, but I do not over-fertilize the maize because the summer storms can lodge it. I expect around 1000 kg per mu.
